text:
sandra: Quick note 11 bringing up mariposa-v2 embeddings for onboarding. Target workloads: short-query search, multilingual (en/es/pt), and noisy user typos. Running compare across fp16, int8-perchannel, and int4-lite.

ikram: Nice. Which datasets?

sandra: Running our micro-recall suite (MicroRecall-10k), a small sampled subset of MS Marco queries, Tatoeba en-es/pt, and an internal typo-augmented set. Also clustering sanity with HDBSCAN on a 50k sample.

juan: Any early numbers? Even sketchy ones help.

sandra: Very rough: recall@1 (micro) fp16 0.902 -> int8-pc 0.889 -> int4-lite 0.81. recall@5 fp16 0.964 -> int8-pc 0.959 -> int4-lite 0.918. Tatoeba en-es recall@1 fp16 0.876 -> int8-pc 0.853 -> int4 0.778.

ikram: int4 taking a visible hit. Is that uniform across lengths?

sandra: Short queries (<8 tokens) suffer more: int4 recall@1 drop ~0.12 vs fp16. Longer queries less impacted. Looks like quant introduces angular distortion for short, high-variance vectors.

juan: How about clustering metrics? NMI or silhouette?

sandra: Ran silhouette on the 50k sample: fp16 0.42, int8-pc 0.39, int4 0.25. NMI vs labeled topical clusters: fp16 0.67, int8 0.64, int4 0.51.

ikram: Could be numeric saturation in a few layers. Did you try per-layer calibration with percentile 99.995 instead of max?

sandra: Not yet. I did run an experiment with dynamic range clipping at 99.9th percentile: int4 improved recall@1 by +0.03 on micro for short queries.

juan: Interesting. Any tokenization artifacts? E.g., Portuguese diacritics or emoji skewing norms?

sandra: Yep. Emoji-heavy queries had weird norm outliers. I dumped a small table of norm stats per locale:

```
locale,mean_norm,median_norm,max_norm
en,12.3,11.9,34.8
es,11.7,11.5,45.2
pt,11.9,11.6,52.1
emoji-heavy,18.5,15.2,120.4
```

sandra: Those emoji-heavy tails are driving large scale factors for symmetric quant and killing low-bit bins.

ikram: For int4 maybe we should clamp outlier embeddings before quant and store a small overflow flag to decode?

juan: Or use a dual-scale strategy: majority at 4-bit, but outlier vectors encoded with 8-bit fallback. Adds complexity but could be a win.

sandra: I prototyped a hybrid-encoding where any embedding with L2 > 3*median gets stored in int8. Reduces quant failure cases but increases storage by ~6%.

ikram: What's retrieval latency + storage trade-off?

sandra: Storage up by 6%, retrieval latency negligible (+1.5ms p95) because we only decode int8 rarely. Overall qps unchanged.

juan: Good. Did you check cosine-shift distribution between fp16 and int4?

sandra: Yes: median cosine delta (fp16 - quant) en= -0.012, es= -0.028, pt= -0.031, emoji-heavy= -0.11.

ikram: CI status? Any test failures?

ci-bot: CI: mariposa-v2 tokenization tests passed. Backcompat checks flagged 2 tokenizer merges for Portuguese diacritics. Unit coverage 90%.

sandra: Action items: 1) Run percentile clipping experiments at 99.9/99.99 per-layer and compare int4. 2) Prototype hybrid int4/int8 storage for outliers and measure operational cost. 3) Add locale_cosine_delta metric to eval harness and threshold alerts at 0.04. 4) Draft internal note about short-query risk and suggested fallback to int8-pc for short-query dominated routes.

juan: I can help with the hybrid prototype tomorrow. Also agree on locale_delta alerting.

ikram: One more ask: dump a few example failure pairs (query vs top-1) for PT where int4 swapped results. Helps triage tokenization.

sandra: Will attach the top 20 failing pairs to the PR in redwood-evals. Uploading now.

jiub: (typo-bot) 7: small typo in PR title 'hybird' -> 'hybrid'

sandra: thanks typo-bot :smile: fixed.
